A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same study with readable main text, equations, 17 tables, four figures, and Appendices A-B. Content can be reliably matched despite table relocation and text reflow.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original Dyck-grammar and CodeLlama experiments. Appendix B includes additional ablations, error analyses, diversity measurements, and out-of-distribution evaluations.

after.justification: V2 retains the original experimental outcomes in Section 5 and Appendix B, including accuracy, query complexity, diversity, and ablation results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same verification, backtracking quota and stride, and argmax regeneration. The generator and verifier constructions are unchanged; the added related-work discussion introduces no implemented component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Dyck-grammar completion and Python list-append test-case generation, including the same bracket-distribution and function-name shifts. No additional dataset or test scenario is evaluated.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain nucleus sampling, temperature scaling, greedy decoding, block best-of-n, and the same verifier controls. Newly cited FUDGE and SynCode are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: Splits, model sizes, hyperparameter searches, metrics, and evaluation procedures are unchanged. These include the 10,000 unseen Dyck prompts and 800 requested CodeLlama test cases per run.

E4.justification: The verifier ablations, backtracking-necessity analysis, error analysis, diversity tests, distribution shifts, and argmax ablation are retained. Appendix B.1.3 now links released code but presents no additional analysis within the PDF.

E5.justification: Both retain ten repetitions for synthetic-verifier validation, five-run standard errors for the main comparisons, and the same diversity aggregation across 100 prompts. No statistical reporting procedure changes.

E6.justification: Corresponding numerical results and qualitative findings in Tables 1-17 and Figures 1-4 are unchanged. For example, Table 8 retains Acc_distinct = 0.714 ± 0.011 for Q = B = 4, top-p = 0.95, and temperature = 1.0.

T1.justification: Definitions 1-9, Theorems 1-2, Propositions 1-2, their proofs, and the knapsack discussion in Appendix A.2 are unchanged. The added probabilistic-verifier discussion introduces no formal result or revised assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about verifier-enabled tractability and backtracking's benefits for query efficiency, accuracy, and diversity.

C2.justification: The added Section 6 calibration warning reiterates a concern already stated in v1's conclusion; probabilistic verifier outputs were also discussed in Section 2. Result interpretations and the query-efficiency limitations in Appendix A.1 remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V1's Appendix B.1.3 promises a future code release. V2 reports that the code is released and supplies a repository link there and in an abstract footnote. Implementation and hyperparameter descriptions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds FUDGE by Yang and Klein (2021) when discussing probabilistic verifiers, and SynCode by Ugare et al. (2024) when relating Dyck grammar to context-free grammar generation. These are limited additions to research positioning and references.

P1.justification: V2 adds short related-work and code-availability passages, expands funding acknowledgements, and corrects 'trained verifies' to 'trained verifiers.' The overall section and appendix structure is retained.

P2.justification: Tables 6 and 7 move from pages 12 and 13 to pages 13 and 14, with accompanying text and footnote reflow. All four figures are identical. V2 also introduces a stray 'sampling' above Table 2.

improvement.justification: V2 replaces a future code-release promise with concrete access information and improves research context through the FUDGE and SynCode connections. These modest gains in reproducibility documentation and positioning outweigh the small typesetting regression above Table 2. Methods, theory, and experimental evidence remain unchanged.
